title: Prospective Root-Candidate Competition Graph, Near-Equal Legal-Move Survival/Elimination Causality, Root-Child Search-Exposure Attribution, PV Branch-Replacement Mechanisms & Preference-Boundary Reconstruction
founding_question: Why does an engine prefer one near-equal legal root move over another under a frozen search regime?

fresh_worlds.eligibility: standard legal nonterminal chess; not in check; plies 14-23; 18-48 legal moves; absolute material imbalance <=3 pawns; disjoint from all recoverable P1-P12 candidate hashes

candidate_qualification.legal_move_universe: enumerate every legal root move; no tactical prefilter
candidate_qualification.shallow_rank: one cold root-restricted equal-node search per legal move; rank by side-to-move engine score with deterministic UCI tiebreak
candidate_qualification.confirmatory_score: two cold root-restricted equal-node repeats for each shortlisted move
candidate_qualification.stability_rule: both confirmatory scores must be non-mate cp scores and exactly equal
candidate_qualification.contextual_winner: the 80k-node shared-search bestmove after the frozen P12 history protocol
candidate_qualification.winner_admission: contextual winner must be a stable shortlisted move
candidate_qualification.rival_rule: among other stable shortlisted moves, choose the move with minimum absolute confirmatory cp difference from the contextual winner; ties prefer higher cp then lexical UCI
candidate_qualification.rationale: restores the early C3X rule that candidate preference must be qualified by independent root-restricted equal-node evidence rather than treating a shared bestmove or MultiPV ordering as explanation.

root_child_attribution.method: privately fingerprint each shortlisted legal move by a cold searchmoves trace; map unique ply-1 internal position keys back to UCI move identity; use that map only to attribute shared-search ply-1 semantic events
root_child_attribution.node_allocation_claim: not made; event exposure is a root-child search-exposure observable, not per-candidate node accounting

exact_target.candidate_membership: target ply-1 key must privately map to the frozen winner or frozen rival
exact_target.selection: lexicographically smallest exact address IDs up to max_targets_per_world, using baseline trace only
exact_target.intervention: T_ONLY exact semantic-use removal; TT storage/replacement/index/age remain untouched

preference_boundary.direct_pair_flip: baseline contextual winner W becomes the frozen near-equal rival R under T_ONLY
preference_boundary.third_move_redirect: T_ONLY selects a legal move other than W or R

claim_ceiling: A DIRECT_PAIR_FLIP identifies an exact search-event-sensitive engine preference boundary between two independently qualified near-equal legal moves under the frozen engine, history and node budget.
Root-child event exposure is not candidate-specific node allocation and must not be described as such.
An engine preference boundary is not objective chess truth, human strategic intent, or a cognitive mechanism.
Cross-engine/source/position transport is claimed only when the frozen replication rule is satisfied.
Raw TT keys remain private intra-run locators and are never emitted in public artifacts.
forbidden: No target selection based on T_ONLY root changes.
No replacement of root-restricted qualification by MultiPV rank.
No public raw TT key emission.
No promotion from local engine preference to human chess explanation.
stop_rule: Adjudicate the frozen 48-world campaign once. If pairwise boundary transport fails, return the result as a transport ceiling rather than subdividing targets after outcomes.
